terms.meaning: South India: the land from the Vindhya mountains to Kanyakumari.
A centre of learning like a residential school. Talagunda and Balligave had the main ones.
A tall pillar, a special contribution of the Gangas.
The ceremony for Gommateshwara at Shravanabelagola, held once every 12 years.

items.name: Beginning of the Shatavahanas
items.formula: First dynasty of the Deccan, between the Godavari and Krishna; once vassals of Chandragupta Maurya.
items.example: Simukha became independent and made Srikakulam his capital.

items.name: Gautami Puthra Shatakarni
items.formula: The greatest Shatavahana; drove out the Sakas and is linked to the Shalivahana Saka.
items.example: Title: Trisamudratoyapitavahana. Yajnashri Shatakarni was the last king.

items.name: Shatavahana society and culture
items.formula: No varna discrimination, women in high posts, trade at Nasik, Kalyan, Broach and Bhatkal.
items.example: Hala wrote Gathasaptashati in Prakrit; Ajanta and Amaravati paintings date from this time.

items.name: The chaitya at Karle
items.formula: Built by Bhootapala, a merchant of Banavasi.
items.example: Shatavahanas followed the Vedic tradition but supported Buddhism and Jainism.

items.name: Mayuravarma
items.formula: Insulted by the Pallava king Shivaskanda Varma, Mayurasharma took up arms and founded the Kadamba kingdom.
items.example: First dynasty of Karnataka, with capital Banavasi (North Canara).

items.name: Kadamba-era inscriptions
items.formula: Halmidi: first Kannada inscription (5th century). Talagunda: first Sanskrit inscription in Karnataka. Malavalli: Prakrit.
items.example: The Chandravalli inscription says Mayuravarma raised the Chandravathi lake wall.

items.name: Kadamba contributions
items.formula: About 300 years of political unity; foundation of Karnataka architecture at Banavasi.
items.example: Court language first Prakrit, later Sanskrit; Kannada was the people's language.

items.name: Ganga capitals
items.example: Gangawadi began with Dadiga and had 27 kings.

items.name: Durvinita
items.formula: The famous Ganga king: built irrigation lakes (Nallala inscription).
items.example: He wrote Shabdavatara and translated Gunadhya's Vaddakathe into Sanskrit.

items.name: Gommateshwara at Shravanabelagola
items.formula: A 58 foot monolith set up by Chavundaraya, minister of Rachamalla IV.
items.example: Bahubali, youngest of 100 brothers, gave up the kingdom he had won from Bharata.

items.name: Ganga temples
items.formula: Kapileshwara at Manne, Pataleshwara and Maruleshwara at Talakad, Kolaramma at Kolar.
items.example: Also the Nageshwara temple at Begur.

items.name: Ganga-era books
items.formula: Sree Purusha: Gajashastra. Shivamara II: Gajashtaka. Chavundaraya: Chavunda Purana.
items.example: Nemichandra: Dravyasara Samgraha. Hemasena: Raghava Pandaviya.

mistakes.text: The Shatavahanas were the first in the Deccan, but the Kadambas were the first dynasty of Karnataka.
Chavundaraya installed Gommateshwara as a minister; he was not the king.
Halmidi is the first Kannada inscription; Talagunda is the first Sanskrit one in Karnataka.
